verdict.rationale: Warp documents programmatic surfaces: a public OpenAPI spec, an "API, CLI, SDK and MCP" platform claim, API keys for headless Oz CLI and cloud-agent use, and a settings file for programmatic control. Coverage is mainly cloud-agent operation, not the whole UI. The docs also show a parity gap: agent profiles must be created in the Warp app and then referenced by ID from the CLI. missing for 10: evidence of API coverage for desktop terminal/UI features (sessions, Warp Drive editing, code editor, themes), API-side creation of agent profiles, and independent or hands-on confirmation of UI-to-API parity.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: API, CLI, SDK and MCP built as a platform, not a vertical product or AI teammate.
The Automation Platform runs cloud agents from triggers, schedules, integrations, and APIs.
API keys let the Oz CLI, cloud agents, and self-hosted workers authenticate without human interaction.
Use it to start agents locally or in the cloud, connect MCP servers, configure integrations, and authenticate without requiring the Warp desktop app.
we are shipping a (long-overdue) settings file so that users and agents get programmatic control over settings and easy portability between devices.
